To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the solution conformation of the peptide melanostatin in the neutral and the protonated forms of dimethylsulfoxide is not a beta-turn structure as suggested earlier.

the backbone of melanostatin has no beta-turn structure in DMSO and that Leu NH in both the forms of the molecule is buried in the hydrophobic pocket formed by the proline side chain and Leu side chain.

melanostatin (PLG) in DMSO solution adopts a backbone con-formation such that leu amide proton is burried by the proline-ring and the side-chain of leucine, and that the key residues involved in this conformational preference are proline and leucine.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the conformational preference of the side chain of Leu in neutral and protonated melanostatin in different solvents.
the conformational preference of the Leu side chain and not the backbone conformation of melanotropin.
the solution conformation of peptides and proteins in the presence of various solvents and in different pH conditions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
melanostatin adopts a conformation such that Leu NH is buried by the ring of proline and the side chain Leu.
melanostatin is a random coil in both the forms of DMSOd and in CDCl3.

the backbone conformation of melanostatins in neutral and protonated form is such that the side chain of the leucine residue is directed towards the backbone and the amide protons of leucine is buried.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the conformational preference of the Leu side chain is not dependent on solvent polarity but on the hydrogen bonding capability of the solvent.
Leu NH in melanostatin is buried in both the forms and in both the solvents, DMSO and CDCl3.
in DMSO the conformation of melanostatine is such that Leu NH is buried and in CDCl3 Leu NH is exposed.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the backbone of melanostatin adopts different conformations in DMSO, CDCl3 and water.
the conformational preference of the Leu residue is the same in the neutral and charged forms of the peptide.
the conformation of Leu side-chain in melanostatin is not sensitive to the pH of the solution.
